title: Gravity and Colony
premise: Beatrix Sterling, a memory-smuggler hauling contraband recollections through contested orbits, intercepts a distress beacon in a dead language and discovers an erased colony: the Meridian, massacred two centuries ago, its records rewritten by the very corporation that now rules the shipping lanes. As corporate enforcers close in, Beatrix must decide whether to sell the evidence to the highest bidder or broadcast it and burn her own carefully hidden past, which turns out to be entangled with the Meridian's fate. In the end, Beatrix sacrifices her smuggled fortune and her anonymity to transmit the colony's memories to every station in the system, choosing truth and love—her bond with archivist Juno Okonkwo—over survival in the shadows.
about_author: Ada Sandoval is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of listening to voices lost at sea. She writes from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where she collects obsolete recording formats.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Beatrix runs a routine smuggling run through orbital customs, hiding stolen memories inside her ship's black-box archive. POV: Beatrix. Establishes her cynical code and her fragile partnership with Juno. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: A distress signal arrives in Meridian Standard, a language extinct for two hundred years. Beatrix, whose grandmother spoke it, translates fragments describing fire and betrayal. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition, the past knocking.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequence
chapters.summary: Corporate inspector Vane boards the ship hunting the illegal signal. Beatrix bluffs her way through an inspection while Juno secretly copies the beacon data. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve, first spark of trust.

chapters.title: What the Records Deny
chapters.summary: In a gray-market archive, Beatrix and Juno find official history: the Meridian colony never existed. But a corrupted memory-cylinder contains a survivor's final recollection of the massacre. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief for people she never met.

chapters.title: Buyer's Market
chapters.summary: A syndicate broker offers a fortune for the cylinder—then reveals the corporation already knows Beatrix has it. POV: the broker. Emotional beat: temptation and the sick realization that invisibility is gone.

chapters.title: The Name in the Cylinder
chapters.summary: Decoding the survivor's memory, Beatrix finds her grandmother's name among the Meridian crew—she is descended from the erased. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade; the massacre becomes personal.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Vane's patrol locks down the station. Juno is captured carrying the cylinder; Beatrix must choose between fleeing with a copy or mounting a hopeless rescue. POV: Juno, under interrogation. Emotional beat: duty versus love, both tested.

chapters.title: Broadcast Zero
chapters.summary: Beatrix hijacks the station's transmitter array to beam the Meridian memories system-wide, but Vane sabotages the uplink mid-transmission. POV: Beatrix. Climax: she burns her ship, her fortune, and her cover as the truth floods outward.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Stations across the system receive the massacre memories; riots and tribunals begin. Beatrix, wounded and exposed, frees Juno from holding. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: exhausted tenderness, the cost made visible.

chapters.title: Gravity and Colony
chapters.summary: Months later, Beatrix—now a witness, no longer a smuggler—testifies as the Meridian is formally restored to history. She and Juno chart a slow route to the colony's ruins. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into purpose; memory, finally, kept.
